title: Moshe Schayek died without a matching donor, and in his wake Ezer Mizion established a bone marrow donor registry

trailer.text: Moshe Schayek was a young man from Afula, and Ezer Mizion, to which he turned for help, is an Israeli organization that has a Cancer Support Division.
Ezer Mizion is an Israeli organization that, according to ynet in 2023, has saved almost 5,000 lives through a Jewish donor database of over 1.2 million potential donors.
According to Israel Hayom (in cooperation with Ezer Mizion), in 1996 the boy Moshe (Moshiko) Sahayek was diagnosed with leukemia and needed a bone marrow transplant.
According to Israel Hayom, the family held two collection drives, no match was found among the approximately 6,000 samples collected, and Moshe died.
The case led to the establishment of Ezer Mizion's bone marrow donor registry.
According to Ynet, in 1998 Dr. Bracha Zisser and Ezer Mizion created the first Jewish donor registry in Israel, to help Jewish patients around the world.

stations.title: A conversation with the doctor at HaEmek Hospital

paragraphs.text: According to David Schayek, he and his wife were called in for a conversation with a doctor at HaEmek Hospital on the day Rabin was assassinated.
In the conversation they were told that their son had blood cancer, leukemia, in a form described as milder.
According to the father, they had four other children at home, the youngest of them two and a half years old.
According to the father, the doctors said that only a bone marrow transplant could save his son's life, and that a suitable donor first had to be found.
According to the father, at that time there was almost no public awareness of bone marrow donation.
According to Ezer Mizion, in 1996 Moshe turned to the organization and asked for help in finding a matching donor.
According to David Schayek, Hadassah Hospital was then the only place in Israel performing compatibility tests, and it could perform only thirty tests per week.
According to the father, he found a laboratory in North Carolina capable of processing 3,000 tests per week.
According to the father, he went from yeshiva to yeshiva and spoke to the students in a nationwide awareness campaign.
According to the article in Hidabroot, Magen David Adom joined the effort and set up blood-testing stations across the country.
According to the father, El Al covered the entire cost of shipping the samples to North Carolina and made sure they were transferred quickly.
According to Ezer Mizion, its Cancer Support Division helped the family organize the sample drive.
In the first drive 2,500 samples were collected, and according to the father the laboratory announced that none of them was a match.
According to the article, Moshe's friends from Midrashiyat Noam insisted on organizing another drive.
According to Israel Hayom, even after the two drives no match was found.

stations.title: Moshe died, and the samples remained

paragraphs.text: According to the father, Moshe died on the 23rd of Cheshvan.
According to the father, after his death he was left with 6,000 samples, and he knew they must not be wasted.
According to the father, when the hospitals showed little interest, he decided to establish the largest Jewish bone marrow registry in the world.
David Schayek turned to Dr. Bracha Zisser, who had supported the family throughout Moshe's illness.
According to Israel Hayom, a few months after his death Moshe's parents asked Moti and Bracha Zisser and Ezer Mizion that the samples serve as the basis for an Israeli national registry.
According to Ezer Mizion, Moshe left a legacy that has enabled dozens of other sick Jews to live.

According to ynet, in 1998 Dr. Zisser and Ezer Mizion created the donor registry, to help Jewish patients around the world. Israel's first bone marrow donor registry had already been opened at Hadassah in 1987.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Bracha Zisser established the registry with her husband, businessman and philanthropist Moti Zisser.
According to ynet, Dr. Zisser's journey began with a personal experience: her husband Mordechai fell ill with leukemia in 1991.
According to Kipa, only 30% of patients find a matching donor among their family members.
According to Kipa, the Jewish people remained separate over the generations and preserved genetic similarity, so the chance of a match between Jews is higher.
According to ynet, the international registry has 44 million potential donors, but very few of them are Jewish.
According to the Times of Israel, before Ezer Mizion joined, the percentage of Jewish samples in the international registry in Leiden, the Netherlands, was frighteningly small.
According to the Times of Israel, the couple conducted mass sample drives, at times collecting over 60,000 samples for a single patient, but still felt they were not reaching certain populations.
According to Ezer Mizion, the registry is affiliated with the American NMDP program and is an accredited member of the WMDA.
According to the Times of Israel, in the past the procedure was painful and performed under general anesthesia.
According to the article in Hidabroot, David Schayek and Bracha Zisser together expanded the registry and worked with the IDF so that every new recruit could join it.
According to ynet, Dr. Zisser came up with the idea that every healthy soldier could join as a donor by giving a sample.
According to Bracha Zisser, she went around the halls of the army for four years, and always ended up facing a legal authority who explained to her that it was impossible.
According to the Times of Israel, by summer 2005 Zisser had given up, and then a friend contacted Elazar Stern, head of the IDF Manpower Directorate.
According to the Times of Israel, Stern stood by the bedside of an Israeli boy who died, and afterwards decided to invite Zisser to his office.
According to Stern, one of the senior army officers argued that at the time of induction soldiers are under too much stress and do not distinguish between an order and a request.
According to the Times of Israel, Stern told the senior officers that the process would begin in three months, and expected them to defend him in court if necessary.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the partnership was agreed upon between the Zissers and Maj.-Gen. Elazar Stern.
According to Kipa, the agreement with the IDF was signed in summer 2005, and since then every recruit can join the registry.
According to the Times of Israel, the sample and the future donation are voluntary and not a mandatory part of the draft.
According to the Times of Israel, nearly seventy percent of draftees agree to provide a sample.
According to Dorit Hazan, director of the Ezer Mizion station in the IDF, 94 percent of flight school candidates agreed to donate.
According to Ezer Mizion, since its establishment in 1998 the registry has handled thousands of search requests from transplant centers in 50 countries.
According to ynet, in 2009 the registry grew through a drive of 62,000 donations, in the case of six-year-old Amit Kadosh.
According to David Schayek in January 2026, 611,957 of the samples in the registry were donated by IDF recruits on their first day of enlistment.
According to the Times of Israel, the collaboration between the IDF and the Ezer Mizion registry recently brought Israel to the highest per capita registration rate in the world.
According to the Times of Israel, soldiers appear to be roughly one and a half times as likely as other Israeli donors to be suitable matches, but the numbers have not yet been fully analyzed.
According to Kipa, in the year before publication 243 lives were saved thanks to a transplant from the registry.
According to Ezer Mizion, it is the largest Jewish registry in the world.
According to the Jerusalem Post, an event at the President's Residence marked 10 years of life-saving partnership between Ezer Mizion and the IDF.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Maj.-Gen. Hagai Topolanski, head of the IDF Manpower Directorate, received a medal for his involvement in the partnership.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Elazar Stern, who was then head of the Manpower Directorate in the army, was a Knesset member at the time the article was written.
According to the Times of Israel, during the Second Lebanon War an F-16 pilot was found to be a match for a two-year-old girl with leukemia.
According to the Times of Israel, Tzvi Lux, a soldier in the Kfir Brigade, received a call from Ezer Mizion four months after enlisting, and he was a perfect match for a sick child.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Erez Raslavsky, a leukemia patient, received a bone marrow transplant from a soldier he had never met.
According to Ezer Mizion, Dr. Bracha Zisser directs the organization's cancer support services, and Ofra Konikoff is the Chief Transplant Coordinator.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Moti Zisser died of cancer three months before the article.
According to David Schayek, every year he holds a memorial for Moshe on the 23rd of Cheshvan.
According to Kipa, although the registry is called national, the state's participation in it is minimal.
According to Israel Hayom, the saliva samples are sent to the United States for decoding, and the decoding cost of each test is 180 shekels.

claims.text: לפי הכתבה, הם הרחיבו יחד את המאגר ופעלו מול צה"ל כדי שכל מתגייס חדש יוכל להצטרף אוטומטית.
claims.quote: Together, they expanded the registry and worked with the IDF so that every new recruit could join automatically.

claims.text: לפי ynet, ד"ר זיסר הייתה זו שהגתה את הרעיון לשתף פעולה עם צה"ל כך שכל חייל בריא יוכל להצטרף כתורם בדגימה.
claims.quote: Dr. Zisser had the idea to work with the Israel Defense Forces to give each incoming healthy soldier the option to become a donor by simply taking a swab to be added to the database.

claims.text: לפי ברכה זיסר, היא שוטטה ארבע שנים במסדרונות הצבא ותמיד נתקלה בגורם משפטי שהסביר שזה בלתי אפשרי.
claims.quote: I bounced around the halls of the army for four years, dozens of offices, and in the end I always landed across the desk from some legal authority who explained to me why it was impossible

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, עד קיץ 2005 זיסר כבר ויתרה, ואז חבר פנה לאלעזר שטרן, ראש אגף כוח האדם בצה"ל.
claims.quote: By the summer of 2005 she’d given up hope. Then a friend contacted Maj.-Gen. Elazar Stern, the head of IDF Manpower at the time.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, אחרי שעמד ליד מיטתו של ילד ישראלי שמת, החליט שטרן להזמין את זיסר למשרדו.
claims.quote: After standing by the bedside of an Israeli boy, the son of a noncommissioned officer, who slowly expired right before his eyes, Stern decided to invite Zisser to his office.

claims.text: לפי שטרן, אחד מבכירי הצבא טען שחיילים בעת הגיוס נתונים ללחץ רב מדי ואינם מבחינים בין פקודה לבקשה.
claims.quote: One contended that soldiers at the time of induction were under too much stress to discern between orders and requests.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, שטרן אמר לבכירים שהתהליך יתחיל בעוד שלושה חודשים וציפה שיגנו עליו בבית משפט במידת הצורך.
claims.quote: Stern thanked them and told them that the process would begin in three months’ time, and that if need be he expected them to be able to defend him in a court of law.

claims.text: לפי Jerusalem Post, השותפות בין עזר מציון לצה"ל סוכמה בין הזוג זיסר לאלוף אלעזר שטרן.
claims.quote: The partnership between Ezer Mizion and the IDF was agreed upon between the Zissers and Maj.-Gen.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, הדגימה ותרומה עתידית וולונטריות ואינן חלק חובה מהגיוס.
claims.quote: onation are voluntary and not a mandatory part of the draft.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, כמעט שבעים אחוז מהמתגייסים מסכימים למסור דגימה.
claims.quote: Nearly seventy percent of draftees agree to provide a sample.

claims.text: לפי דורית חזן, מנהלת תחנת עזר מציון בצה"ל, מועמדי בית הספר לטיסה הסכימו לתרום ב-94 אחוז.
claims.quote: A few weeks ago we had flight school candidates in here and 94 percent of them consented.

claims.text: לפי ynet, ב-2009 במקרה של עמית קדוש בת השש גדל המאגר במבצע של 62,000 תרומות.
claims.quote: In 2009, with the case of 6-year-old Israeli Amit Kadosh, the database again saw substantial growth with a drive of 62,000 donations.

claims.text: לפי דוד סחייק בינואר 2026, 611,957 מהדגימות נתרמו על ידי מתגייסי צה"ל ביום הגיוס הראשון.
claims.quote: Of those, 611,957 were donated by IDF recruits on their very first day of enlistment.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, שיתוף הפעולה בין צה"ל למאגר עזר מציון דחף את ישראל לשיעור הרישום לנפש הגבוה בעולם.
claims.quote: The collaboration between the IDF and the Ezer Mizion Bone Marrow Registry has recently pushed Israel to the highest per capita registry rate in the world.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, נראה שחיילים מתאימים כתורמים בסבירות גבוהה פי אחד וחצי בערך מתורמים ישראלים אחרים, אך המספרים טרם נותחו במלואם.
claims.quote: soldiers appear to be roughly one and a half times as likely as other Israeli donors to be suitable matches for those in need.

claims.text: לפי כיפה, בשנה האחרונה לפני הפרסום ניצלו חייהם של 243 נפשות בזכות השתלה מהמאגר.
claims.quote: בשנה האחרונה לבדה ניצלו חייהם של 243 נפשות בזכות ההשתלה

claims.text: לפי עזר מציון, המאגר שלה הוא המאגר היהודי הגדול בעולם (בעמוד שנתוניו מ-2026).
claims.quote: Today, Ezer Mizion’s Bone Marrow Registry is the largest Jewish registry in the world.

claims.text: לפי Jerusalem Post, אלוף חגי טופולנסקי, ראש אגף כוח האדם בצה"ל, קיבל מדליה על מעורבותו בשותפות להצלת חיים.
claims.quote: Hagai Topolanski, received a medal for his personal involvement in the Saving a Life Partnership, and for encouraging IDF recruits to give something of themselves, and in that way, restore a whole world.

claims.text: לפי Jerusalem Post, שטרן היה אז ראש אגף כוח האדם בצבא וכיום הוא חבר כנסת.
claims.quote: Elazar Stern, who was then head of the Manpower Directorate in the army, and who is now a Knesset member.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, במלחמת לבנון השנייה נמצא טייס F-16 כמתאים לילדה בת שנתיים חולת לוקמיה.
claims.quote: In fact, during the Second Lebanon War an F-16 pilot was found to be a match for a two-year-old girl with leukemia

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, צבי לוקס, חייל בחטיבת כפיר, קיבל טלפון מעזר מציון ארבעה חודשים אחרי הגיוס.
claims.quote: Four months later, while on leave from basic training, the half-Brazilian, half-Israeli infantryman received a call from Ezer Mizion.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, לוקס היה התאמה מושלמת לילד חולה.
claims.quote: He was a perfect match for a sick young child.

claims.text: לפי Jerusalem Post, ארז רסלבסקי, חולה לוקמיה, קיבל השתלת מח עצם מחייל שמעולם לא פגש.
claims.quote: The upshot was that he received a bone marrow transplant from a soldier whom he had never met, but to whom he now owed his life.

claims.text: לפי עזר מציון, ד"ר ברכה זיסר מנהלת את שירותי התמיכה בחולי סרטן בארגון ואופרה קוניקוף היא רכזת ההשתלות הראשית.
claims.quote: Under the direction of Dr. Bracha Zisser, Director of Ezer Mizion’s cancer support services and Ofra Konikoff, Chief Transplant Coordinator

claims.text: לפי דוד סחייק, מדי שנה הוא עורך אזכרה למשה ב-23 בחשוון.
claims.quote: Each year, David holds a memorial for Moshe on the 23rd of Cheshvan.

claims.text: לפי כיפה, אף שהמאגר מוגדר לאומי, השתתפות המדינה בו מזערית.
claims.quote: למרות שהמאגר מוגדר כמאגר לאומי של מדינת ישראל, ההשתתפות של המדינה היא מזערית

claims.text: לפי ישראל היום (בשיתוף עזר מציון), דגימות הרוק נשלחות לארצות הברית לפענוח, ועלות פענוח כל בדיקה היא 180 שקלים.
claims.quote: מכאן הן נשלחות לארצות הברית כדי לעבור פיענוח ולהצטרף למאגר

claims.text: לפי כיפה, במבצע מיוחד נאספו 5,000 דגימות דם, לא נמצאה התאמה והנער נפטר.
claims.quote: במבצע מיוחד נאספו 5,000 דגימות דם. למרבה הצער, לא נמצאה ההתאמה המיוחלת, והנער הלך לעולמו.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, אלעזר שטרן הוא הקצין שיזם את התוכנית עם צה"ל.
claims.quote: said Maj. Gen. (res) Elazar Stern, the officer who initiated the program.

claims.text: לפי עזר מציון, נכון ל-1 בנובמבר 2026 כולל המאגר יותר מ-1,315,627 תורמים פוטנציאליים.
claims.quote: As of November 1, 2026, the Bone Marrow Registry has grown to include more than 1,315,627 potential donors!

claims.text: לפי דוד סחייק בינואר 2026, המאגר כולל 1,480,210 דגימות.
claims.quote: According to David, the registry, now recognized as the Jewish global bone marrow database, currently includes 1,480,210 samples.

claims.text: דוד סחייק, אביו של משה, אמר בראיון מינואר 2026 ל-Hidabroot ש-3,765 אנשים חיים כיום בזכות המאגר שהוקם.
claims.quote: Three thousand seven hundred and sixty-five people are alive today thanks to the bone marrow registry we established.

claims.text: לפי עזר מציון, המאגר סייע ב-6,819 השתלות מצילות חיים (בעמוד שנתוניו מנובמבר 2026).
claims.quote: Ezer Mizion’s Bone Marrow Registry has facilitated 6,819 lifesaving transplants, saving the lives of patients throughout the world

claims.text: לפי עזר מציון, נכון ל-1 בדצמבר 2021 המאגר סייע ב-4,227 השתלות תאי גזע.
claims.quote: Ezer Mizion’s Bone Marrow Registry has facilitated 4,227 stem cell transplants, saving the lives of patients throughout the world

claims.text: לפי הרב חנניה חולק, מייסד עזר מציון, המאגר סייע להציל 2,200 חיים, מהם 1,100 בזכות תרומות חיילי צה"ל.
claims.quote: The Ezer Mizion bone marrow registry has been instrumental in saving 2,200 lives, of which 1,100 were saved through IDF donations, said Ezer Mizion founder Rabbi Chananya Chollak.

claims.text: לפי כיפה, המאגר הוא השישי בגודלו בעולם והמאגר היהודי הגדול ביותר בעולם.
claims.quote: ומדובר במאגר השישי(!) בגודלו בעולם, ובמאגר היהודי הגדול ביותר בעולם

claims.text: לפי ישראל היום (בשיתוף עזר מציון), המאגר הוא החמישי בגודלו בעולם והמאגר היהודי הגדול בעולם.
claims.quote: הוא החמישי בגודלו בעולם והמאגר היהודי הגדול בעולם

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, 40 אחוז מתרומות מח העצם דרך עזר מציון הלכו ליהודים בחו"ל.
claims.quote: Currently 40 percent of all bone marrow donations given through Ezer Mizion go to Jews living abroad.

claims.text: לפי ד"ר זיסר בכתבת ynet מ-2023, 60% מההתאמות הן עם חולה מחוץ לישראל ו-40% בתוך ישראל.
claims.quote: 60% are matched with a patient outside of Israel.

claims.text: לפי ynet, ב-1998 יצרו ד"ר זיסר ועזר מציון את מאגר התורמים, כדי לעזור לחולים יהודים בעולם. מאגר תורמי מח העצם הראשון בישראל נפתח עוד ב-1987 בהדסה.
claims.quote: In 1987, it opened Israel's first Bone Marrow Donor Registry

quote_translations.c28: In 1996 the youth Moshe (Moshiko) Schayek, of blessed memory, was diagnosed with leukemia and needed a bone marrow transplant
quote_translations.c21: Against the clock of life that was running out, they held two sample collection drives, but sadly, among all the approximately 6,000 samples collected in these drives the hoped-for match was not found, and Moshe died.
quote_translations.c30: together with Ezer Mizion the national bone marrow donor registry, with the aim of enlarging the pool of potential Jewish donors
quote_translations.c41: In summer 2005 the agreement with the IDF was signed, and since then every recruit can join the registry
quote_translations.c27: and asked that the samples that had been collected and tested not go to waste but serve as the basis for establishing an Israeli national registry of potential bone marrow donors
quote_translations.c31: Only 30% of patients manage to find a matching donor among their family members.
quote_translations.c32: Fortunately for us, the Jewish people remained separate over the generations, and thereby preserved genetic similarity.
quote_translations.c75: In the last year alone the lives of 243 people were saved thanks to the transplant
quote_translations.c66: Although the registry is defined as a national registry of the State of Israel, the state's participation is minimal
quote_translations.c67: From here they are sent to the United States to undergo decoding and join the registry
quote_translations.c29: In a special drive 5,000 blood samples were collected. Sadly, the hoped-for match was not found, and the youth passed away.
quote_translations.c63: and this is the sixth(!) largest registry in the world, and the largest Jewish registry in the world
quote_translations.c64: it is the fifth largest in the world and the largest Jewish registry in the world
